deploy-bot: terraform apply started for workspace `prod-dc9-gpupool`
deploy-bot: repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/infra.git commit: 9f4b2c7 tag: v1.7.8 user: infra-automation
deploy-bot: plan URL: https://ci.internal.redwood/plan/4567 (apply locked to change window until 2026-03-02T22:00Z) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

jason: noted, i'll run quick smoke checks against canary nodes once this finishes
maria: change window confirmed, we're good until 22:00 UTC
carol: watching prometheus dashboard for dc9 gpupool, will ping if anything odd :eyes:

deploy-bot: terraform apply completed in 2m12s
deploy-bot: ```Apply complete! Resources: 1 added, 2 changed, 0 destroyed.
Outputs:
  gpupool_size = "32"
  runtime_image = "redwood/runtime:v2.3.1"
```

jason: saw an unexpected instance_type drift in the apply logs — nodes changed from `p4d.24xlarge` -> `p3.16xlarge` in the `gpupool` resource, that wasn't in the plan notes.
sylvia: hmm that suggests the autoscaler or provider mapping flipped. can someone check the provider alias map? might be a TF var override from the module registry.
maria: @oncall can you verify whether the infra-image-pin was applied? i'd prefer to pin runtime image rather than rely on instance type drift. if it's a provider bug we should rollback the gpupool change.
oncall: looking — checking cluster API and cloud console now. will report back in 2m.

oncall: confirmed: the provider mapping for `region: dc9` had a stale mapping in SSM that translated `gpu_preference: best_performance` -> p3 instead of p4. this applied during the reconcile after the apply.

jason: given that, i recommend revert gpupool instance_type to previous commit and pin `runtime_image` to `v2.3.0` for safety.
maria: agreed. rollback gpupool change and pin runtime_image to `v2.3.0` — deploy-bot can you start a revert apply with tag `v1.7.8-revert-gpupool`? include a plan for review.
deploy-bot: initiating revert plan: branch infra@revert/9f4b2c7-gpupool 
deploy-bot: plan URL: https://ci.internal.redwood/plan/4580 (revert plan)

maria: quick note for postmortem: add a step to validate provider SSM mappings before apply in the change window runbook.

deploy-bot: revert apply started for workspace `prod-dc9-gpupool` (tag: v1.7.8-revert-gpupool)
deploy-bot: revert apply completed in 1m05s
deploy-bot: ```Apply complete! Resources: 1 added, 3 changed, 0 destroyed.
Notes: gpupool instance_type pinned back to p4d.24xlarge, runtime_image set to redwood/runtime:v2.3.0
```

jason: thanks — i'll re-run smoke checks and validate metrics over the next 10m
carol: dashboards look stable so far, will keep monitoring
maria: closing loop: will add provider mapping validation to runbook and add an alert on SSM mapping drift. good catch everyone :clap:
